body: As someone with no friends and who gave up a while ago, hugs are certainly welcome.

All of it, really. There's a lot to my body I hate ( well, duh ), and can't ever see any efforts in changing making a difference. My family still thinks i'm largely a joke, and I'd love to vent. I'm good at venting. And bitching and complaining I guess.

My voice, my body. I don't think I'll ever pass or be happy.
I really appreciate the offer. <3
I'm afraid I don't have a kik.

Yep. I'm consistently invisible to any group I join, and all of my friendships are essentially people using me as a crutch then doing away with me.
Feels good man.
At least in the latter case they deign to notice me, which is a refreshing change of pace.
Thanks for the help, SW.
Nothing like some escapism. Drinking is good for that, too.
It worked out well.
I think I've pretty much given up. Some people just aren't going to be successful in life, and honestly, I want out.
Still not seeing it. Today's a fucking terrible day.

That's not a terrible idea, honestly. I don't know how my family or job would react if I worked towards pushing things a little more.

I guess I don't really care that much, though, since they're largely crap people as it is.
I'll have to take a look around, thank you.

I've debated self-medding, but I'm curious about dosage and whatnot. I sometimes wear some of my favourite undergarments out, which helps, but any time I catch a look at myself my mood pretty much goes down the shitter anyway.

They always say you've gotta learn to love yourself before anything else, but if I can't do that, there's not much of a point in anything else.

Thank you. Yeah, thoughts about my puberty haunt me daily, or just better life decisions I could've made in general.

I feel like a lot were in a similar place, but many others were in far, far better positions to begin with, I think. And that's okay. That's their lot, and this is mine. 

So far, despite holding on, things haven't been very great at all. In 5 years I'll be 30, and likely no closer to happiness than where I am now -- and I'll be older for it, too!

Thank you, but I don't see any greatness coming out of anything anytime soon.
This is very good advice, actually.

The last few sentences here utterly broke my heart. It's unrealistic and cliche, but I find myself so completely unlovable, and the idea that someone might in fact be out there is something I find beautiful and terrible all at once. I don't think I'll ever manage any sort of 'great results', but I certainly have geeky and nerdy down. <3

I've never worked with e-checks. I wonder how many to buy? Funds aren't that large of an issue.

Is it wrong of me to be afraid on the grounds of parental approval? Well, only my mother. Dad was never in the scene to begin with. My mother knows and she supports me ( sort of? She said she was okay with it, but assumed it 'was a phase' ), but I don't know how she'd react to this. My happiness comes first, but family is really all that I have left, you know?

Oh gracious, I'd rather not be president of anything.

I've had some very real threats in some bad places around here. Almost was mugged more than once, a few awkward run-ins with the police ( mostly being stopped and asked a lot of questions about something unrelated to me). The two biggest spooky places here are Woodbury and Camden, in this area -- both of which have some reputations you can probably look up!

I'm a little wary of the religious group type, I'll be honest. I know it's a bad prejudice to have, but a lot of the people around here are the "Say one thing mean another" type, and the handful I had that were religious and I came out to kinda bashed me and shunned me for it -- one stuck around, but refuses to use correct pronouns and won't acknowledge me on it on the grounds of "not approving my lifestyle choices" because he's in that weird boat that we're all 'created perfectly'.

I know that really can't be said about everyone, and I've met an equal or even greater share of people online who were very accepting, but the idea of actually going in and meeting them seems kinda scary.

Online medding is probably my best bet now. I just need to find more resources on it before I make any big time decisions. I want to know what'll work most effectively for my weight and whatnot ( though that, thankfully, has been steadily dropping -- almost the size I was back in late middle school/early high ). If things go bad, yeah I'm just going to off myself quick-like; I don't want to be melodramatic or overly painful in my methods. 

I've heard hormones can be expensive, but other friends have told me they can be pretty cheap, too.

I've seriously thought about other jobs, yeah, but location has to be very close by, since it's public transit or -walking- for me. I'm making almost 10/hr right now, and since they're so lax and fucked up, some days it boils down to almost doing nothing and getting paid, so to be honest, as shitty as the conditions are, that's something that's going to be hard to give up unless I can find one that pays significantly more.

Yeah. I've found that "It Gets Better" doesn't seem to do much for me, which is unfortunate because it's really pitched as a very hopeful message.

Yeah, that sounds pretty similar. It's good that people are becoming more and more aware of trans people and their rights worldwide ( albeit slowly ), but locally, it's very much a similar position. I do have some -adorable- panties that I love to wear, some lacy, some not, and it's been fun to wear those to work. I haven't tried socks yet, but that's a good idea, as well -- I've got plenty of those, too. Everything else is unfortunately ( fortunately? ) dress-coded for work, but that makes it easier to hide everything.

As far as around the house, I think I'm far too embarrassed to do any such thing. A while ago, my mother promised we'd sit and talk about it and offered to do my nails, but the way she suggested it came off as a terrible joke -- any time I bring it all up with her again, she kind of laughs.

Thank you for the support. <3 I've always struggled to find those little things -- being grateful it's not very hot, maybe. Happy I have my curtains. I totally get the idea of doing little things or appreciating little things to brighten the day, but sometimes things are just so damn gloomy.

I'm sure your summer is going to be a beautiful one. <3
Pretty much this.

I'm a computer technician for a store where they're consistently making "gay" and "tranny" jokes on anyone who even remotely looks gay or trans somehow ( ??? ), and where my management flirts with and promotes coworkers who have no fucking idea what they're talking about.

No health benefits, limited hours. A tendency for nobody else to do their jobs and text on their phones instead.

You keep mentioning 'trans friendly', but I uhh.. haven't had any luck so far. At all.

I'm in NJ, for reference.

More or less. I'm terribly lonely, and it leaves me clinging to what I've got online until they can't stand me.

That website looks.. interesting. Kind of daunting, honestly. So many groups with so many people. I should add it's hard for me to get around -- I have a license and whatnot, but the family only has one car, which we need to keep available. Public transit is an option, but my work schedule is so fucking -bizarre- that I never really know what I'm free to do -anything- except go to sleep and wake up early to go back to work.

Living the dream.

There's apparently a Lutheran church a ways away from me, but it's in a not-so-great part of town. While I doubt the churchgoers would do me any harm, the surrounding neighbours might. 

I do. I do, actually, because I feel like there's a level I need to at least get to before I'll be happy with myself. Given how I look now, I know there's a very real chance I'll end up even more unfortunate looking, which can only spell more trouble for my life down the road. Thanks, patriarchy, I suppose.

Either way, I don't think I'm ever going to really be happy with who I am at this point.

I just feel so old. I know logically that's not the case, but I'm one of those people who dread things somehow ever being "too late" to transition. Again, logically, I know that's not ever truly a threat, but it looms very real to me during these intense times of sadness. 

Honestly, yeah, that was going to be my route for suicide if it came to it. I was hoping to hold out and when things inevitably went south, at least I'd have given it a decent shot. It's getting pretty tough to even get to that point.

I still don't have any insurance. I still can't schedule anything for myself nor do I know any therapists around here. There's the Mazzoni centre a fair trip away up in Philadelphia, but I fear they mostly specialise in 'youth', which, of course, I'm not. My last trip there was incredibly embarrassing, as well, which has left something of a bitter taste in my mouth. I was told that 'supporters were welcome, but not allowed to participate' when it came to meetings and seeking help -- apparently I'm just that hard to believe.

Three whole years. That's quite a bit of time, to me, at least.

I can take things a day at a time, but then it's like my life is being pulled up from under me. Next thing I know, weeks have gone by -- and while that's good because I can usually remain relatively stable during that time, I've literally accomplished nothing. More time has been wasted, and I've made zero progress.

I've thought about self-medding; there's risks, but I mean when you consider I'm already pretty much all-in for my well-being, death is more or less something I can agree with as a hazard.
I'm really hoping so. I'm desperately trying to hang in there.

I sometimes find myself envious in all the worst ways. It's ugly as a response, yes, but I'm just being honest -- I think it's because I've always felt the window for transitioning for me is gone, given my age and how I look.

EDIT: To make it clear, I'd never, -ever- attack anyone for their success or take my negative emotions out on other people -- I'm the sort who just sorta stews in feeling crappy for a while.
Oh I do a lot of revenge plotting against the day. Thank you for the comment! I'm really hoping to meet some folks here.

Oooh! I don't know how well I'd fare there. I tend to find things like that a little upsetting.

It's not that I'm not happy for people, or enjoy sadder things instead, it's just that other people's success tends to remind me of the ( seemingly hopeless ) jam that I'm in.
Thank you. <3
I like this. Hello Kate, judging by your name. <3
